For an integrable density $f$ whose root belongs to $\mathcal D_\omega^0$, \cref{prop:integrable-threshold-adjoints} will give a similar representation for $F\mapsto\log b_\omega(\mathrm{e}^Ff)$. That functional is defined by a subsolution threshold; its construction does not require an exact equation for $f$ or prescribe a singularity type.

The uniform tail criterion in \cref{prop:root-uniform-tails} identifies the closure $\mathcal D_h^0$ of bounded roots. For densities with roots in this space, \cref{thm:integrable-current-attainment,prop:integrable-threshold-adjoints} give an attained compact Gauduchon dual problem and absolutely continuous supporting probabilities. The trace errors along smooth maximizing sequences tend to zero in total variation by \cref{prop:threshold-trace-saturation}. A smooth strictly positive maximizer would force threshold subsolutions to differ only by constants; attainment by a singular current does not supply that elliptic argument. Whether the approximation condition also suffices for the exact equation in \cref{qu:individual-equation-threshold} remains to be determined. When $v_-(h)=0$, even equality $\mathcal D_h^0=\mathcal D_h$ is not established here.

\Needspace{16\baselineskip}
\section{Integrable densities in the compact Gauduchon problem}
\label{sec:integrable-gauduchon-currents}

Retain $n\geq2$, the Hermitian background $\omega$ and the probability volume $\mathrm{d}V$. For $T\in\mathscr G_\omega$, write $\Gamma_0(T)=k_T\,\mathrm{d}V$ as in \cref{thm:gaud-determinant-subcritical}. If $p\geq0$ is measurable, define
\[
 D_p(T)=\int_Xp k_T\,\mathrm{d}V,
\]
allowing $+\infty$. For a smooth positive normalized Gauduchon form this is the test $L_{\omega,\gamma}(p)$. The space $\mathcal D_\omega^0$ from \cref{prop:root-uniform-tails} supplies a class of unbounded weights for which compactness still gives attainment.

\begin{theorem}\label{thm:integrable-current-attainment}
For every nonnegative $p\in L^n$,
\begin{equation}\label{eq:integrable-current-supremum}
 \sup_{T\in\mathscr G_\omega}D_p(T)=\rho_\omega(p),
\end{equation}
with $+\infty$ allowed. If $p\in\mathcal D_\omega^0$, the functional $D_p$ is finite, concave and weakly upper semicontinuous on $\mathscr G_\omega$. Its maximum is attained, and the measures $p k_T\,\mathrm{d}V$, as $T$ ranges over this set, have uniformly integrable densities.
\end{theorem}
\begin{proof}
For a smooth strictly positive $p$, \cref{thm:weak-gaud-compact-duality} applied to $F=n\log p$ proves \eqref{eq:integrable-current-supremum}. By \cref{thm:gaud-determinant-subcritical}, for every $r>n$,
\begin{equation}\label{eq:current-root-test-bound}
 \sup_{T\in\mathscr G_\omega}\int_X|q| k_T\,\mathrm{d}V
       \leq C_r\|q\|_{L^r}.
\end{equation}
Approximate a bounded nonnegative $p$ in $L^{2n}$ by smooth strictly positive functions. This estimate and \eqref{eq:root-subcritical-bound} give uniform convergence of the current functionals and convergence of the root norms. Thus the supremum formula holds for bounded $p$. Their current functionals are also upper semicontinuous and concave, by \cref{lem:weak-gaud-determinant-dual} and uniform convergence. For general $p\in L^n$, monotone truncation gives
\[
 \sup_T D_p(T)=\sup_T\sup_K D_{\min(p,K)}(T)
       =\sup_K\rho_\omega(\min(p,K))=\rho_\omega(p).
\]
Only two suprema have been interchanged; this step alone gives no attainment.

Now suppose $p\in\mathcal D_\omega^0$. By the supremum formula applied to the tail,
\[
 0\leq D_p(T)-D_{\min(p,K)}(T)
 \leq \rho_\omega(p\mathbf1_{\{p>K\}})\longrightarrow0
\]
uniformly in $T$. Hence $D_p$ is finite and a uniform limit of upper semicontinuous concave functionals. Compactness of $\mathscr G_\omega$ gives a maximizer. Finally, fix $1<q<n/(n-1)$. For every measurable $E$,
\[
 \sup_T\int_Ep k_T\,\mathrm{d}V
 \leq\rho_\omega(p\mathbf1_{\{p>K\}})
       +K C_q\,\mathrm{d}V(E)^{1-1/q}.
\]
Choosing first $K$ and then the volume of $E$ proves uniform absolute continuity. The total masses are bounded by $\rho_\omega(p)$, so the densities are uniformly integrable.
\end{proof}

A maximizing current is a finite positive $\ddc$-closed current. The theorem asserts neither a smooth minimizing Gauduchon metric nor an exact Monge--Amp\`ere solution at the subsolution threshold. These are different attainment questions.

\subsection{Supporting probabilities for an integrable density}

Let $f\in L^1$ be nonzero and nonnegative, and assume $p=f^{1/n}\in\mathcal D_\omega^0$. For a continuous real $F$, set
\[
 B_f(F)=\log b_\omega(\mathrm{e}^Ff)
       =-n\log\rho_\omega(p \mathrm{e}^{F/n}),\qquad
 M_f(F)=\rho_\omega(p \mathrm{e}^{F/n}).
\]
Both quantities are finite and $M_f(F)>0$, by the order-ideal property. Let $\mathscr M_f(F)$ be the currents maximizing $D_{p \mathrm{e}^{F/n}}$, and put
\[
 \nu_{T,F}=\frac{p \mathrm{e}^{F/n} k_T}{M_f(F)}\,\mathrm{d}V
 \quad(T\in\mathscr M_f(F)).
\]
These are probability measures. Define $\mathcal A_f(F)$ to be all Borel probability measures satisfying
\begin{equation}\label{eq:integrable-threshold-support}
 B_f(G)\leq B_f(F)-\int_X(G-F)\,\mathrm{d}\nu
 \qquad(G\in C(X,\mathbb R)).
\end{equation}

\begin{proposition}\label{prop:integrable-threshold-adjoints}
The functional $B_f$ is concave, decreasing and $1$-Lipschitz for the uniform norm, and $B_f(F+a)=B_f(F)-a$ for constants $a$. Moreover,
\[
 \mathcal A_f(F)=\{\nu_{T,F}:T\in\mathscr M_f(F)\}.
\]
This set is nonempty, convex and weakly compact. Its measures are absolutely continuous. For each $R>0$, their densities, with $\|F\|_\infty\leq R$, are uniformly integrable. For $H\in C(X,\mathbb R)$, its one-sided derivatives satisfy
\[
 (B_f)'_+(F;H)=-\max_{\nu\in\mathcal A_f(F)}\int_XH\,\mathrm{d}\nu,
 \qquad
 (B_f)'_-(F;H)=-\min_{\nu\in\mathcal A_f(F)}\int_XH\,\mathrm{d}\nu.
\]
\end{proposition}
\begin{proof}
For each $T$, H\"older's inequality makes $F\mapsto\int_Xp \mathrm{e}^{F/n}k_T\,\mathrm{d}V$ logarithmically convex. Taking suprema preserves the inequality defining logarithmic convexity. Thus $B_f=-n\log M_f$ is concave. Order and homogeneity give the translation rule and, by comparison with constant translates, the Lipschitz estimate.

We check the compactness needed to identify all supporting measures. Suppose $T_j\to T$ and $D_{p \mathrm{e}^{F/n}}(T_j)\to M_f(F)$. Upper semicontinuity makes $T$ a maximizer. For a continuous real $H$, choose $\varepsilon>0$ with $1\pm\varepsilon H>0$. The weights $p \mathrm{e}^{F/n}(1\pm\varepsilon H)$ lie in $\mathcal D_\omega^0$. Apply the preceding theorem to both weights and pass to any weak cluster point of $p \mathrm{e}^{F/n}k_{T_j}\,\mathrm{d}V$. Its mass is $M_f(F)$, so the two signs force its integral against $H$ to equal that of $p \mathrm{e}^{F/n}k_T\,\mathrm{d}V$. Hence the weighted measures converge. Matrix determinant concavity gives
\[
 p \mathrm{e}^{F/n}k_{tT_1+(1-t)T_2}\,\mathrm{d}V
 \geq t p \mathrm{e}^{F/n}k_{T_1}\,\mathrm{d}V
       +(1-t)p \mathrm{e}^{F/n}k_{T_2}\,\mathrm{d}V.
\]
For two maximizing currents, equal total masses turn this into equality. The set $\mathscr N_f(F)$ of displayed probabilities is therefore nonempty, compact and convex.

A maximizing $T$ gives
\[
 M_f(G)\geq M_f(F)\int_Xe^{(G-F)/n}\,\mathrm{d}\nu_{T,F}.
\]
Jensen's inequality proves \eqref{eq:integrable-threshold-support}, so $\mathscr N_f(F)\subset\mathcal A_f(F)$. For the reverse inclusion, the derivative argument of \cref{thm:gaud-current-all-adjoints} applies with the finite measure $p k_T\,\mathrm{d}V$ in place of $k_T\,\mathrm{d}V$. Explicitly, uniform Taylor expansion gives
\[
 D_{p \mathrm{e}^{(F+tH)/n}}(T)
 =D_{p \mathrm{e}^{F/n}}(T)+\frac tn\int_X H p \mathrm{e}^{F/n} k_T\,\mathrm{d}V+O(t^2),
\]
where the error is uniform in $T$ since $D_{p \mathrm{e}^{F/n}}(T)\leq M_f(F)$. Testing maximizers at $F$ bounds the right difference quotients of $M_f$ from below. Maximizers at $F+tH$ are near-maximizers at $F$, by the uniform multiplicative bounds, so the preceding convergence of weighted measures gives the reverse bound. Consequently
\[
 (B_f)'_+(F;H)=-\max_{\nu\in\mathscr N_f(F)}\int_XH\,\mathrm{d}\nu.
\]
Every $\nu\in\mathcal A_f(F)$ satisfies
$\int_XH\,\mathrm{d}\nu\leq\max_{\sigma\in\mathscr N_f(F)}\int_XH\,\mathrm{d}\sigma$ for all continuous $H$, by its supporting inequality. Separation from a compact convex set yields $\nu\in\mathscr N_f(F)$. Replacing $H$ by $-H$ proves the left-derivative formula.

Finally $M_f(F)\geq \mathrm{e}^{-R/n}\rho_\omega(p)$ when $\|F\|_\infty\leq R$. Thus the displayed probability densities are at most $\mathrm{e}^{2R/n}\rho_\omega(p)^{-1}p k_T$. The uniform integrability in the preceding theorem proves all the stated absolute-continuity assertions.
\end{proof}

When $f=1$, this is the zero-reference construction of \cref{chap:normalization}. For general $f$, the functional is defined by the maximal subsolution coefficient; it does not presume exact equation existence. No prescribed-singularity analogue is inferred from this Hermitian-background argument. Under positive lower mass, every nonnegative $L^1$ density satisfies the root-space hypothesis. Without that property, the uniform tail condition gives an explicit sufficient hypothesis for this compact dual description.

\subsection{Trace inequalities at the subsolution threshold}

A smooth Gauduchon test pairs with the full positive current $\omega+\ddc u$, even when the extended Monge--Amp\`ere mass of $u$ is infinite. The mixed inequality relates this finite linear pairing to the density threshold.

\begin{lemma}\label{lem:unbounded-gauduchon-trace-density}
Let $u\in\PSH(X,\omega)$ and $0\leq g\in L^1(\mathrm{d}V)$ satisfy
$\mathrm{MA}^{\mathrm{ext}}_\omega(u)\geq g\,\mathrm{d}V$. For every smooth Hermitian form $\gamma$,
\[
 (\omega+\ddc u)\wedge\gamma^{n-1}
       \geq(g\,\mathrm{d}V/\gamma^n)^{1/n}\gamma^n.
\]
The left side is the ordinary current paired with a smooth form; it retains any trace mass on the pole set of $u$.
\end{lemma}
\begin{proof}
We first verify the bounded version with two different smooth backgrounds. Suppose $w\in\PSH(X,\omega)\cap L^\infty$ and $\mathrm{MA}_\omega(w)\geq q\,\mathrm{d}V$, where $q\geq0$. On a sufficiently small coordinate ball centered at $x$, let $\kappa$ be the Euclidean form and put $\beta=\omega(x)$, $\eta=\gamma(x)$. Given $\varepsilon>0$, shrink the ball so that
\[
 \omega\leq\beta+\varepsilon\kappa\leq\omega+2\varepsilon\kappa,
 \qquad
 \gamma\leq\eta+\varepsilon\kappa\leq\gamma+2\varepsilon\kappa.
\]
Add to $w$ a quadratic potential of $\beta+\varepsilon\kappa$, and take a quadratic potential of $\eta+\varepsilon\kappa$. Both are bounded plurisubharmonic functions on the ball. Their top-degree measures dominate $q\,\mathrm{d}V$ and $\gamma^n$, respectively. The local mixed inequality used in \cref{lem:nonclosed-mixed-density}, namely \cite[Theorem 1.2]{Dinew09}, gives
\[
 (\omega_w+2\varepsilon\kappa)\wedge
             (\gamma+2\varepsilon\kappa)^{n-1}
 \geq(q\,\mathrm{d}V/\gamma^n)^{1/n}\gamma^n.
\]
For each $\varepsilon$ the small balls cover a fixed coordinate chart. The displayed measures depend polynomially on $\varepsilon$, with coefficients of locally finite variation. Let $\varepsilon\downarrow0$ to obtain the bounded inequality.

Translate $u$ to be nonpositive and put $u_k=\max(u,-k)$. By locality and positivity,
$\mathrm{MA}_\omega(u_k)\geq\mathbf1_{\{u>-k\}}g\,\mathrm{d}V$. Apply the bounded inequality to $u_k$. These functions converge to $u$ in $L^1$, so the linear currents $\omega+\ddc u_k$ converge to $\omega+\ddc u$, and their wedges with the fixed smooth $\gamma^{n-1}$ converge weakly. The right sides tend in $L^1$ to the asserted density: the pole set has zero smooth volume, and $g^{1/n}$ is integrable. Passing to the measure inequality proves the result. No convergence of the undamped top-degree measures was used.
\end{proof}

\Needspace{25\baselineskip}
\begin{proposition}\label{prop:threshold-trace-saturation}
Let $0\leq f\in L^1$ be nonzero and $b=b_\omega(f)>0$, and write $p=f^{1/n}$. Suppose $u\in\PSH(X,\omega)$ satisfies $\mathrm{MA}^{\mathrm{ext}}_\omega(u)\geq bf\,\mathrm{d}V$. For every smooth strictly positive $T\in\mathscr G_\omega$, the measure
\[
 R_{u,T}=(\omega+\ddc u)\wedge T-b^{1/n}p k_T\,\mathrm{d}V
\]
is positive and has mass
\[
 R_{u,T}(X)=1-b^{1/n}D_p(T).
\]
In particular, if $(T_j)$ is a smooth maximizing sequence for $D_p$, then $\|R_{u,T_j}\|_{\mathrm{TV}}\to0$, uniformly over all such threshold subsolutions $u$.

If also $p\in\mathcal D_\omega^0$ and $T_j\to T$ as currents, then $T$ maximizes $D_p$ and
\[
 (\omega+\ddc u)\wedge T_j
       \rightharpoonup b^{1/n}p k_T\,\mathrm{d}V.
\]
For a fixed current limit $T$, this limiting probability is independent of the threshold subsolution $u$ along the same sequence.
\end{proposition}
\begin{proof}
A smooth strictly positive $T$ is $\gamma^{n-1}$ for a Gauduchon metric $\gamma$. The normalization is $\int_X\omega\wedge T=1$. The preceding lemma proves positivity of $R_{u,T}$; distributional Stokes gives $((\omega+\ddc u)\wedge T)(X)=1$. This proves the mass formula. Since $\rho_\omega(p)=b^{-1/n}$, a maximizing sequence makes this nonnegative mass tend to zero. It equals the total variation norm and is independent of $u$.

Under the tail hypothesis, the near-maximizer argument in the proof of \cref{prop:integrable-threshold-adjoints}, with $F=0$, gives
$p k_{T_j}\,\mathrm{d}V\rightharpoonup p k_T\,\mathrm{d}V$ and shows that $T$ maximizes. Add the error measures, which tend to zero in total variation. The resulting probability is $\nu_{T,0}$ of that proposition.
\end{proof}

The limiting formula is stated along smooth maximizing sequences. It does not define the product $(\omega+\ddc u)\wedge T$ for an arbitrary singular current $T$, or assert independence of the chosen maximizing current.

\Needspace{10\baselineskip}
\begin{corollary}\label{cor:smooth-dual-threshold-rigidity}
If $D_{f^{1/n}}$ has a smooth strictly positive maximizer in $\mathscr G_\omega$, all subsolutions at the threshold $b_\omega(f)>0$ differ by constants. In particular, when $f$ is smooth and strictly positive, every threshold subsolution is a constant translate of the smooth solution of
$\mathrm{MA}_\omega(v)=b_\omega(f)f\,\mathrm{d}V$.
\end{corollary}
\begin{proof}
For a smooth strictly positive maximizing $T$, the preceding error measure has mass zero and therefore vanishes. Two threshold subsolutions $u,v$ satisfy $\ddc(u-v)\wedge T=0$. This is a homogeneous scalar elliptic equation with smooth coefficients. Elliptic regularity makes $u-v$ smooth, and the maximum principle on the connected compact manifold makes it constant. If $f$ is smooth and strictly positive, \cref{thm:gaud-volume-dual-formula} supplies the required maximizing Gauduchon form from the smooth solution. That solution is a threshold subsolution by \cref{prop:individual-normalizer-lp}.
\end{proof}

boundaries: No BMP or positive lower mass for the root-tail criterion, integrable-current supremum or trace density inequality.
Current attainment and uniformly integrable determinant-weighted measures require the bounded-root closure hypothesis; no smooth maximizer is inferred.
Smooth dual attainment gives uniqueness of threshold subsolutions up to constants through a fixed elliptic equation.
No exact equation for general L1 data, arbitrary singular-current wedge, or prescribed-singularity extension is asserted.
